content.text:
I submitted index 28 (Sb 0.67, Y 0.33) as the best composition. It had the highest EQE I measured, but only 0.0035%. Every composition I measured was close to zero, so I can't tell whether this is near the library's best.

All three merit measurements are used. I measured the middle and both ends of the library:

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 23 | 0.52 | -0.00014 (about zero) |
| 3 | 0.07 | 0.0008 |
| 28 | 0.67 | 0.0035 |

- **Index 23 was my first pick and failed.** It is the closest candidate to YSbO4, which the models predicted to be stable with a band gap (2.97 eV) small enough to absorb the 3.2 eV light. But its X-ray pattern didn't match YSbO4, or any other known phase in this system.
- **Why Sb-rich is plausible:** the band-gap model puts the antimony-rich oxides well below 3.2 eV (Sb2O4 1.67 eV, Sb6O13 2.05 eV), and yttrium oxide far above (5.57 eV). That fits EQE rising with Sb content.
- **Main caveat:** index 28 is the most Sb-rich composition on offer, so the trend doesn't point to anything better than it. I didn't measure indices 24–27; I judged them unlikely to beat 28. I spent the last measurement on the unexplored Y-rich end (index 3) instead, which came in below 28.

X-ray patterns at indices 14, 23 and 28 all showed the same cubic structure, so the whole composition line seems to be one phase. I used 3 of the 5 X-ray measurements.
